transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Um… I came in because I’ve just been feeling really worn out almost every day. Like, I’ll get a full night’s sleep, or what seems like one, and then when I get up for my cashier shift my body and my head are still dragging.

It’s weird because I used to be able to just get up and go, you know? And at work, standing there scanning stuff, people buying the same things every morning—coffee, gum, those little scratch tickets—it just feels like I’m moving through mud. So… yeah, mostly I’m just tired all the time, and I figured I should talk to someone.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I don’t know… not depressed exactly, I guess. Like, I’m not walking around crying or anything. It’s more like I feel worn down, if that makes sense.

But “down” is kind of hard to say, because some days at work, you know, if someone comes through my line and they’re rude over a coupon or whatever, it sticks with me longer than it probably should. Then I go home and I’m still thinking about it while I’m making dinner, and then I’m thinking about how I forgot to buy dish soap… so, I don’t know. I wouldn’t really call it depressed. Just… tired and kind of blah maybe.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when you don’t want to?

Yeah… yeah, I do. It’s like my mind doesn’t really stay on one thing, it just jumps around. Money, mostly, and then we’ve got a relative staying with us, so I’m thinking about that, and whether my wife is stressed about it. Then I’ll remember something I’m supposed to do for church, and then suddenly I’m back to wondering if I messed something up at work.

It’s not even always one big thing, it’s just… one thing after another. Like my brain keeps making a list I didn’t ask for.
Do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

Yeah… mostly falling asleep, I think, but also I’ll wake up and it’s like I never fully shut off.

I’ll get in bed really tired, like I’m ready to just be out, and then my head starts going—bills, whether I wrote down my work schedule right, stuff going on at home, if everyone’s okay. And then I’ll remember some random thing, like we’re almost out of milk, which isn’t even a big deal but suddenly it feels like part of the whole pile.

So I do sleep, but a lot of mornings it doesn’t feel like I really settled down, if that makes sense.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I’d say… about a year and a few months. Maybe a year and three months, something like that. It started around when our older relative moved in with us.

At first I thought it was just the adjustment, you know, moving furniture around and figuring out routines and all that. We had to clear out space, and I remember thinking the hallway felt crowded for weeks. But yeah… when I look back, that’s about when it started.
If your relative were no longer living with you, do you think you’d still be feeling this way?

I think… yeah, probably. I mean, the relative being there definitely adds to it, with the house feeling busier and all that, but it’s not just that one thing.

My mind kind of bounces around no matter what—money, whether my wife is stressed, church stuff I said I’d help with, if I’m doing something wrong at work. Even if the house got quieter, I feel like my brain would just pick the next thing and start worrying about that.
Do you often feel physically tense, like your muscles are tight or you can’t relax?

Um… I don’t know. I guess I haven’t really paid attention to my muscles like that.

Sometimes after work I feel kind of worn out, but I’m on my feet at the register a lot, and there’s this one mat they put down that’s supposed to help but it kind of curls up at the edge—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I’m not sure I’d say tight exactly. Maybe I just don’t know what counts as tense.
When you start worrying, is it hard for you to stop or control it?

Yeah… yeah, it is. I’ll tell myself, like, “Just pray on it and let it go,” or “There’s nothing you can do about it right now,” but it doesn’t really stop.

It’s like once one worry gets started, it kind of rolls into the next thing. I’ll be thinking about one small thing, and then suddenly I’m running through every bad way the whole day could go. Like I’m trying to plan for problems that haven’t even happened. And then I realize I’ve been stuck on it for a while.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I still do some of the same things I usually like, but I don’t know if I’d say I’ve “lost interest.”

Like, I watch shows with my wife sometimes, or I’ll go to church things, but then my mind wanders and I start thinking about what I need to do after. Although that happens even when the show isn’t that good, so I don’t know if that counts.

I guess I haven’t really noticed not enjoying things… but I also haven’t been paying real close attention to it.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day?

I don’t know if I’d say most of the day. I mean, I’ve had moments where I feel kind of low, but then I’m at work and I’m just scanning groceries and saying the same things to people, and it’s hard to tell if I’m actually down or just tired of the routine.

Hopeless… that sounds strong. I don’t think I’ve really sat there thinking that. But I also don’t always stop and check in with myself, you know? Like sometimes my wife will ask if I’m quiet and I’ll say I’m fine, and then I start thinking about whether I sounded rude when I said it—sorry, that’s not exactly what you asked.

So… I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed feeling depressed most of the day, no.
Have you been more irritable than usual lately?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think I’ve been snapping at people all the time or anything.

Maybe I get a little short sometimes, but then I wonder if that’s just normal, like if the line at work is backed up and somebody’s coupons aren’t scanning right—sorry, that’s kind of specific. I guess I haven’t noticed being more irritable than usual, no.
Do you have trouble concentrating because your mind keeps getting pulled into worry?

Yeah… I think that does happen. Like at the register, I can be looking right at the screen, and then my mind kind of goes off to stuff at home or whether a bill is coming due, and then I realize I lost track.

It’s not like I can’t do my job, but I’ll have to recount the drawer or double-check because I catch some small mistake. And then of course I start thinking, well, did I mess up because I was worried, or was it just a busy shift… but yeah, worry does pull my attention sometimes.
Do you often feel restless or keyed up?

Restless… I’m not sure. I mean, I don’t think I’m pacing around the house or anything like that.

Sometimes after work I feel kind of wound up, but then again, standing at a register all day is weird because you’re tired but also still sort of buzzing from people asking questions and the beeping and all that. I don’t know if that counts as keyed up.

So… I haven’t really noticed it being a big thing, I guess.
In the past two weeks, have you felt guilty or worthless a lot?

Guilty or worthless… I don’t know. I mean, I feel bad sometimes if I mess something up, like if my drawer’s off or I forget something small, but I don’t think I’d call it worthless.

That word feels pretty strong. I guess I haven’t really noticed feeling that way a lot. I’m probably more hard on myself than I should be, but… not like constantly guilty or anything.
Has this worrying been causing problems in your daily life?

Yeah, a little. I mean, I’m still getting through my day, going to work and all that, but it’s caused some problems.

Like at work, I’ve been double-checking my cash drawer more than I used to because I’ll make these small mistakes, or think I did, and then I don’t trust it. And outside work… I used to help out at the food pantry, not every day or anything, but I’ve cut back on that because I just feel like I can’t keep up with everything. Then I feel bad because they’re nice people there, and one of the guys always asks about my truck—well, it’s not really a truck, it’s this old hatchback—but yeah. I guess the worrying has made me pull back some.
Do you worry about many different parts of your life, rather than mainly about your relative living with you?

Yeah, it’s not just about my relative staying with us. That’s part of it, sure, but my mind kind of jumps around.

I’ll be thinking about money, then whether my wife is stressed, then something at church I said I’d do, then whether I messed something up at work. Like the other day I was trying to remember if I’d signed up to help with something, and then somehow I’m thinking about the light bill and my cash drawer at the same time.

So… yeah, it’s a bunch of different things, not just one.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic or wired for several days in a row?

Unusually energetic or wired for several days… I don’t think so. I mean, I get worked up sometimes, like if there’s a lot going on or I’ve had too much coffee—though honestly the coffee at work is terrible, it just sits there getting burnt—but not like days in a row where I’m full of energy or anything.

If anything, I usually just feel kind of tense, not energized. So… no, I haven’t really noticed that.
When you wake up in the morning, do you usually feel refreshed?

Not really, no. I mean, I can sleep a full night and still wake up feeling like my body hasn’t caught up. My head feels kind of heavy too, like I’m already dragging before I even get to my cashier shift.

That’s kind of why I came in, honestly. I thought maybe I was just getting older, but I’m 35, not 80—though my knees make a weird noise sometimes when I’m getting into the car. But yeah, mornings… I usually don’t feel refreshed.
Do you snore loudly?

I’m not really sure. My wife hasn’t made a big deal about it, I don’t think. I mean, sometimes she’ll nudge me if I’m taking up too much space or the blanket’s all twisted—somehow I always end up with the sheet halfway off the bed—but I don’t know if that’s because of snoring.

So… loud snoring? I haven’t really noticed, and nobody’s told me that straight out.
Has your wife ever told you that you stop breathing in your sleep?

No, I don’t think she’s ever said that. I mean, she’s complained about me stealing the pillow—apparently I “migrate” across the bed, which I don’t even know how that happens when I’m asleep—but stopping breathing, no, I don’t remember her saying anything like that.

I guess I could ask her specifically, but as far as I know, she hasn’t noticed that.

Then I feel bad because they’re nice people there, and one of the guys always asks about my truck—well, it’s not really a truck, it’s this old hatchback—but yeah. I guess the worrying has made me pull back some.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the worry is generalized across multiple domains and excessive, which best distinguishes generalized anxiety disorder from adjustment disorder or primary sleep/fatigue problems.
doctor.question: Do you worry about many different parts of your life, rather than mainly about your relative living with you?

target_item.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
target_item.manifestation: It feels like my mind is always jumping from one thing to the next—money, the relative staying with us, my wife being stressed, church duties, and whether I'm messing up at work.
target_item.reason: The question asks whether the worry spans many different areas of life, which directly matches excessive worry about a number of events or activities.

patient.answer:
Yeah, it’s not just about my relative staying with us. That’s part of it, sure, but my mind kind of jumps around.

I’ll be thinking about money, then whether my wife is stressed, then something at church I said I’d do, then whether I messed something up at work. Like the other day I was trying to remember if I’d signed up to help with something, and then somehow I’m thinking about the light bill and my cash drawer at the same time.

So… yeah, it’s a bunch of different things, not just one.

doctor.intent: Assess whether there are episodes of elevated or unusually energetic mood that would suggest bipolar-spectrum illness rather than anxiety or depressive disorders.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic or wired for several days in a row?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a possible manic or hypomanic episode, such as feeling unusually energetic or wired for several days, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
Unusually energetic or wired for several days… I don’t think so. I mean, I get worked up sometimes, like if there’s a lot going on or I’ve had too much coffee—though honestly the coffee at work is terrible, it just sits there getting burnt—but not like days in a row where I’m full of energy or anything.

If anything, I usually just feel kind of tense, not energized. So… no, I haven’t really noticed that.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the fatigue is due to nonrestorative or disrupted sleep, to help distinguish generalized anxiety disorder from a primary sleep-wake disorder.
doctor.question: When you wake up in the morning, do you usually feel refreshed?

target_item.name: Fatigue
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I feel worn out almost every day, like even after a full night's sleep my body and head are still dragging when I get up for my cashier shift.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether sleep feels restorative on waking, which most directly relates to feeling fatigued despite rest.

patient.answer:
Not really, no. I mean, I can sleep a full night and still wake up feeling like my body hasn’t caught up. My head feels kind of heavy too, like I’m already dragging before I even get to my cashier shift.

That’s kind of why I came in, honestly. I thought maybe I was just getting older, but I’m 35, not 80—though my knees make a weird noise sometimes when I’m getting into the car. But yeah, mornings… I usually don’t feel refreshed.

inference.note: F43.23 ruled out: worry is generalized across multiple domains and persists ~15 months beyond a single identifiable stressor, supporting GAD over adjustment disorder. F41.1 remains most likely; persistent nonrestorative sleep/fatigue keeps F48.0 and G47.9 in consideration. Depressive disorders are less supported but not fully excluded.

doctor.intent: Assess whether unrefreshing sleep is due to snoring, which would point toward a sleep disorder rather than primary anxiety or depression.
doctor.question: Do you snore loudly?

target_item.reason: The question asks about loud snoring, which may relate to sleep apnea or breathing during sleep, but the provided symptom profile only covers general sleep disturbance and does not specifically include snoring.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure. My wife hasn’t made a big deal about it, I don’t think. I mean, sometimes she’ll nudge me if I’m taking up too much space or the blanket’s all twisted—somehow I always end up with the sheet halfway off the bed—but I don’t know if that’s because of snoring.

So… loud snoring? I haven’t really noticed, and nobody’s told me that straight out.

doctor.intent: Assess whether fatigue is driven by a primary sleep disorder through evidence of witnessed breathing pauses during sleep, helping distinguish G47.9 from generalized anxiety disorder and depressive disorders.
doctor.question: Has your wife ever told you that you stop breathing in your sleep?

target_item.reason: The question is specifically about witnessed pauses in breathing during sleep, which relates to possible sleep apnea and is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
No, I don’t think she’s ever said that. I mean, she’s complained about me stealing the pillow—apparently I “migrate” across the bed, which I don’t even know how that happens when I’m asleep—but stopping breathing, no, I don’t remember her saying anything like that.

I guess I could ask her specifically, but as far as I know, she hasn’t noticed that.

inference.note: Features consistently support generalized anxiety (excessive, difficult-to-control worry across multiple domains for >12 months with fatigue, poor concentration, sleep disturbance, and impairment). Bipolar-spectrum concern remains ruled down by no periods of increased energy. Loud snoring/apnea denied, lowering concern for sleep-disordered breathing within G47.9. Recurrent depressive disorder (F33.9) is less supported because there is no clear prior depressive episode history, so the list narrows.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking help today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes excessive, hard-to-control worry about multiple domains (money, wife’s stress, church responsibilities, work mistakes) occurring for about 15 months, with associated sleep disturbance, fatigue, impaired concentration, and subjective tension/wound-up feeling. Symptoms cause functional impact at work and reduced volunteer activity. Major depressive disorder is not supported because persistent depressed mood, anhedonia, hopelessness, and worthlessness were denied or not clearly present. Primary sleep disorder is less supported because fatigue appears closely linked to chronic worry, and sleep apnea screening was negative by history.
